about: Published MLX runs for the Mac Studio M3 Ultra: someone else's Mac and benchmark, never run here. On a Mac the fast engine is MLX, so these are MLX 4-bit models (about 4.5 bits per weight with their scales), not llama.cpp GGUFs. calc() uses a run like a measured one for the same model, compression and prompt, and scales the estimate for the other prompt sizes, compressions and crews from it (tagged 'est. from rep.'). Picked by the Strix Halo's rules: no speculative decoding (no MTP, no draft model, no prompt lookup), one request, the lab's model at 4-bit. Both Macs are the 28-core-CPU, 60-core-GPU M3 Ultra (the lab's 256 GB Mac Studio comes with 60 or 80 GPU cores; the memory runs at 819 GB/s either way). Rapid-MLX's methods page (Mac Studio Mac15,14, 256 GB, macOS 26.5.2, MLX 0.32.2, mlx-lm 0.31.3) gives Qwen3.8 27B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with a cold prefix cache at 92-, 2,012-, 8,156- and 32,732-token prompts, 256 tokens out, median of three: the question (300 tokens) takes the 92-token prompt for writing and the 2,012-token prompt for reading (92 tokens are too few to time reading: half a second, mostly fixed cost), the document (8,000) the 8,156-token prompt for both. Reading is prompt tokens divided by the time to the first token. For Qwen3.8 27B the plain-decoding numbers come from release 0.13.3: 0.13.4 turns on the model's MTP head by itself and writes 43.4 tokens/s at 8K (the README's headline), which is speculative decoding. Flash-Next's rows are 0.13.4's default path, the same as 0.13.3's within 0.1 token/s; its 4-bit weights are about 99 GB (the Spark's UD-Q4_K_XL file is 111 GB). Qwen3.6 35B-A3B has one 4-bit M3 Ultra run, an oMLX community benchmark (96 GB, oMLX 0.3.7rc2): its 8K row (2,156 tokens/s reading, 94.5 writing) is used for the document; the same session's 16K to 64K rows write at only 49-52 tokens/s, a drop that a 6-bit session on the same kind of Mac (81.2-81.8 tokens/s at 1K-4K, omlx.ai/benchmarks/jyqet4u4) doesn't show, so those rows are left out. Nothing published for Gemma 4 E4B on an M3 Ultra (NVIDIA's chart has only the 5090's 2.3x lead); it stays estimated.
